label: thm:threshold
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:threshold}
The heavy-ball method with Polyak's tuning converges on every
$f\in\mathcal F_{\mu,L}$ from every initial point if and only if $\kappa<\kappa_c$. More
precisely,
\[
 \rho_{\rm HB}(\kappa)<1\quad(1<\kappa<\kappa_c),\quad \rho_{\rm HB}(\kappa_c)=1,\quad
 \rho_{\rm HB}(\kappa)>1\quad(\kappa>\kappa_c),
\]
and $\rho_{\rm HB}(\kappa)\le\sqrt{\varphi q}$ for $\kappa<\kappa_c$. At $\kappa_c$ a
function in $\mathcal F_{\mu,L}(\mathbb R^3)$ has a trajectory with
$\lVert x_N-x^\star\rVert\ge\lVert x_0-x^\star\rVert/\sqrt5$ for all $N$, which converges
to a three-cycle; above $\kappa_c$ the same construction diverges
exponentially.
head: environment
name: Sharp convergence threshold

label: thm:regularity
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:regularity}
The function $\rho_{\rm HB}$ is continuous and strictly increasing on $(1,\infty)$ and
real analytic outside the five switching points
$\kappa_W<\kappa_1<\kappa_a<\kappa_b<\kappa_2$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:classification}. It is analytic at $\kappa_c$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical}
 \rho_{\rm HB}(\kappa)=1+\frac{\kappa-\kappa_c}{4\kappa_c}+O\bigl((\kappa-\kappa_c)^2\bigr).
\end{equation}
As $q\downarrow0$,
\[
 \rho_{\rm HB}=(1+\sqrt2)\,q-\Bigl(2+\frac{3\sqrt2}2\Bigr)q^2+O(q^3),\quad
 \rho_{\rm HB}-\rho_{\rm sp}=\frac{10+7\sqrt2}{4}\,q^3+O(q^4),
\]
and as $\kappa\to\infty$, $\rho_{\rm HB}(\kappa)\to\rho_*=1.71298\ldots$, the positive
root of $\rho^4-2\rho^3+2\rho^2-2\rho-1$.

body_md:
\label{lem:dualfactor}
For $G\ge1$ and $-1\le c\le1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alphabeta}
 \Phi(c)=(G-c)\bigl\{(1-c^2-u^2)\,\alpha_J-2u(1-c^2)\,\beta_J\bigr\},
\end{equation}
where $\alpha_J\ge1$ and $\beta_J\ge0$ are divided differences of Chebyshev
polynomials that depend on $G$, $c$ and the weights and are independent of
$u$. In particular, for $u'\ge u\ge0$,
\[
 \Phi_{G,u'}(c)\le\Phi_{G,u}(c)-(G-c)(u'^2-u^2).
\]

label: thm:A
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:A}
Assume \eqref{eq:quad}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\par\hangindent 40\p@ If $\Theta(\omega)>\omega/2$ for every $\omega\in(0,\pi]$, then the
method converges.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ If $\Theta(2\pi j/k)\le\pi/k$ for coprime integers $1\le j<k/2$, then
there are $f\in\mathcal F_{\mu,L}(\mathbb R^3)$ and $x_0$ with
$\lVert x_N-x^\star\rVert\ge c\lVert x_0-x^\star\rVert>0$ for all $N$; the trajectory
converges to a $k$-periodic orbit that rotates by $2\pi j/k$ in a plane. If
the inequality is strict, then $\rho>1$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ Let $\Omega_1$ be the set of tunings in \textup{(i)}. On its closure
relative to \eqref{eq:quad}, $\rho\le1$. At every boundary point of
$\Omega_1$ at which $\min_\omega(\Theta(\omega)-\omega/2)=0$ is attained at
$\omega=2\pi/K$, the hypothesis of \textup{(ii)} holds with $j=1$ and $k=K$;
there $\rho=1$, and the point lies on the boundary of the convergence region.
\end{enumerate}

body_md:
\label{thm:B}
Assume \eqref{eq:quad}.

\par\hangindent 40\p@ If $\Theta(\omega)>\omega/2$ on $(0,\pi]$, then the set
$\{r\in(\rho_b,1):H_r(c)\ge0\ \text{for all }c\in[-1,1]\}$ is a nonempty interval
with right endpoint $1$. With $r_1$ its infimum, $\rho_{\rm q}\le\rho\le r_1<1$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ Suppose $\rho_{\rm q}>\sqrt\beta$ and $\Theta(\omega)>\omega/2$ on $(0,\pi]$. Then
$r_1=\rho_{\rm q}$ if and only if $H_{\rho_{\rm q}}(c)\ge0$ for all $c\in[-1,1]$. On the set
$\mathcal Q$ of such tunings, $\rho=\rho_{\rm q}$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ If $\rho_{\rm q}=\sqrt\beta$, then $\rho>\rho_{\rm q}$.
\end{enumerate}

label: cor:C
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:C}
Assume \eqref{eq:quad}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $\mathcal L(-1)=(2+2\beta-x)(2+2\beta-y)>0$ and $\mathcal L(1)=2(1-\beta)(y-x)+xy>0$.
Hence $\Omega_1$ is the set where $\beta=0$, or the vertex
$c_*=(1+2\beta+\beta^2-\beta x-y)/(4\beta)$ lies outside $(-1,1)$, or the
discriminant $(y-1-2\beta-\beta^2+\beta x)^2-4\beta(2-2x+xy+2\beta^2-2\beta y)$
is negative. On the boundary of $\Omega_1$ the tangency frequency is
$\omega_*=\arccos c_*$, and the phase-locked points of
Theorem~\ref{thm:A}\textup{(iii)} are those with $c_*=\cos(2\pi/K)$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ With $c_{jk}=\cos(2\pi j/k)$ and $h_{jk}=\cot(\pi/k)\sin(2\pi j/k)$,
\begin{align*}
 \Theta(2\pi j/k)\le\pi/k&\iff \Xi(c_{jk})\ge h_{jk}\\
 &\iff\mathcal L(c_{jk})\le(y-x)(1-\beta)(1+c_{jk}-h_{jk}).
\end{align*}
For $j=1$ the right side vanishes, and the $K$-tongue is
$\{\mathcal L(\cos(2\pi/K))\le0\}$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ If $\rho_a\ge\rho_b$ and $\rho_{\rm q}>\sqrt\beta$, then with $r=\rho_a$,
$H_r(c)=(1-c)K_\mu(c)$ for a convex quadratic $K_\mu$ with $K_\mu(-1)\ge0$;
within $\Omega_1$ the set $\mathcal Q$ is given there by $K_\mu(1)\ge0$ together with
the vertex-or-discriminant condition for $K_\mu$. If $\rho_b>\rho_a$ and
$\rho_{\rm q}>\sqrt\beta$, then with $r=\rho_b$, $H_r(c)=(1+c)K_L(c)$ for a concave
quadratic $K_L$ with $K_L(1)\ge0$, and within $\Omega_1$ the set $\mathcal Q$ is
given there by $K_L(-1)\ge0$.
\end{enumerate}

label: thm:lattice
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:lattice}
Assume \eqref{eq:quad}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\par\hangindent 40\p@ The conditions \eqref{eq:feasible} are feasible at $t=0$ if and only if
there is a nonzero measure $w\ge0$ on $[0,\pi]$ with $\int\Lambda_n\,dw\ge0$
for all $n\ne0$ and $\int\cos\Theta\,dw\ge0$. In particular feasibility at
$t=0$ depends on the tuning only through the curve $\Theta$, that is, through
the three coefficients of $\Xi$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $\Lambda_n<0$ at a point of $\mathcal C$ if and only if $0<n\xi-\ell\eta<1$ for
some integer $\ell$. The sign of $\Lambda_n$ changes only across the lattice
lines $n\xi-\ell\eta=0$ and $n\xi-\ell\eta=1$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ The points $(2\pi j/k,\pi/k)$ become the lattice points $(j,k)$. The
condition $\Theta(2\pi j/k)\le\pi/k$ says that $\mathcal C$ meets the ray through
$(j,k)$ at or beyond $(j,k)$, and $\Omega_1$ is the set of tunings whose curve
lies in the half plane $\xi<1$.
\end{enumerate}

body_md:
\label{thm:farey}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\par\hangindent 40\p@ The lattice lines $n\xi-\ell\eta=1$ through $(j,k)$ have $n\equiv j^{-1}\pmod k$.
Among them, those with $|n|<k$ are the lower lag $n=b$, whose line also
passes through $(c,d)$, and the upper lag $n=-d$, whose line also passes
through $(a,b)$.

lag $n$ is violated if and only if $jn\bmod k\in\{1,\dots,\lceil k\Theta/\pi\rceil-1\}$.
No lag is violated if and only if $\Theta\le\pi/k$; when $\Theta$ exceeds
$\pi/k$, the first violated lags are $n\equiv b\pmod k$, that is, the parent
lags $b$ and $-d$.
\end{enumerate}

label: def:levels
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:levels}
A tuning satisfying \eqref{eq:quad} is resolved at level $0$ if $\mathcal C$ lies
in $\xi<1$ or meets a ray through a point $(1,K)$ at or beyond that point. It
lies in the gap $I_K$ of level one if the dip $\{\Theta<\omega/2\}$ is nonempty

$\Theta(2\pi/(K+1))>\pi/(K+1)$.

label: thm:fan-div
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:fan-div}
Let $p\ge2$ and $k=k_p=pK+1$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\par\hangindent 40\p@ If there are $w_j\ge0$, $1\le j<k/2$, not all zero, with
$\sum_jw_j\Lambda_n(\omega_j)\ge0$ for $n=1,\dots,k-1$ and
$\sum_jw_j\cos\theta_j\ge0$, then there are $f\in\mathcal F_{\mu,L}(\mathbb R^{2r+1})$, $r$ the number
of nonzero weights, and $x_0$ whose trajectory converges to a $k$-periodic
orbit; in particular $\rho\ge1$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ Let $p\le K+1$, and suppose $\pi/k<\theta_p<\pi p/k$ and
$\pi(p-1)/k<\theta_{p-1}<\pi(K+1)/k$.
Then $\Lambda_1(\omega_p)>0>\Lambda_{-K}(\omega_p)$ and
$\Lambda_{-K}(\omega_{p-1})>0>\Lambda_1(\omega_{p-1})$, and the lags $1$ and $-K$
are satisfied by some measure on $\{\omega_{p-1},\omega_p\}$ if and only if
\begin{multline*}
 \Delta_p:=\sin\tfrac{\pi p}k\,\sin\bigl(\tfrac{\pi p}k-\theta_p\bigr)\,
 \sin\tfrac{\pi(K+1)}k\,\sin\bigl(\tfrac{\pi(K+1)}k-\theta_{p-1}\bigr)\\
 -\sin\tfrac{\pi(p-1)}k\,\sin\bigl(\theta_{p-1}-\tfrac{\pi(p-1)}k\bigr)\,
 \sin\tfrac\pi k\,\sin\bigl(\theta_p-\tfrac\pi k\bigr)\ \ge0 .
\end{multline*}
If moreover $\theta_{p-1}\le\pi/2$, which is automatic for $p\ge3$, and the
lags $n\in\{2,\dots,k-1\}\setminus\{(p-1)K+1\}$ are satisfied for one ratio
$w_{p-1}/w_p$ of the admissible interval, then the conclusion of \textup{(a)}
holds.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ For $p=2$, $k=2K+1$, and $\pi/k<\theta_1,\theta_2\le2\pi/k$, the remaining
lags are satisfied automatically, and the program of \textup{(a)} with the two
harmonics $\omega_1,\omega_2$ is feasible if and only if
\[
 2\cos\tfrac\pi k\cos\tfrac\pi{2k}\,\sin\bigl(\tfrac\pi k-\vartheta_2\bigr)\cos\bigl(\vartheta_1+\tfrac\pi{2k}\bigr)
 \ge\sin\tfrac\pi k\,\sin\vartheta_1\sin\vartheta_2,\quad
 \vartheta_j=\theta_j-\tfrac\pi k .
\]
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f\in\mathcal F_{\mu,L}$ have minimizer $0$ and $f(0)=0$, put $M=L-\mu$ and
$f_0=f-\mu\lVert \cdot\rVert^2/2$. Then $f_0$ is convex and $M$-smooth. Applying the
descent inequality to the convex function $f_0-\langle \nabla f_0(y),\cdot\rangle$, which
is minimized at $y$, gives the cocoercivity inequality
$\langle \nabla f_0(x)-\nabla f_0(y),x-y\rangle\ge M^{-1}\lVert \nabla f_0(x)-\nabla f_0(y)\rVert^2$.
By \eqref{eq:psi}, $\nabla\psi(e)=\frac2M\bigl(\frac{L+\mu}2e-\nabla f(e)\bigr)
=e-\frac2M\nabla f_0(e)$, and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert \nabla\psi(x)-\nabla\psi(y)\rVert^2&=\lVert x-y\rVert^2
 -\tfrac4M\langle \nabla f_0(x)-\nabla f_0(y),x-y\rangle\\
 &\quad+\tfrac4{M^2}\lVert \nabla f_0(x)-\nabla f_0(y)\rVert^2\le\lVert x-y\rVert^2 .
 \end{aligned}
\]
Moreover $\psi(0)=0$ and $\nabla\psi(0)=0$. Conversely, if $\psi\in\mathcal S$, then
$\nabla f=\frac{L+\mu}2\mathrm{id}-\frac{M}2\nabla\psi$ satisfies
$\langle \nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\ge\frac{L+\mu}2\lVert x-y\rVert^2-\frac M2\lVert x-y\rVert^2=\mu\lVert x-y\rVert^2$
and $\lVert \nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\rVert\le\frac{L+\mu}2\lVert x-y\rVert+\frac M2\lVert x-y\rVert=L\lVert x-y\rVert$,
so $f\in\mathcal F_{\mu,L}$; the two maps are inverse to each other. Substituting
$\nabla f(x^\star+e_k)=\frac{L+\mu}2e_k-\frac M2\sigma_k$ in \eqref{eq:hb} gives
$e_{k+1}=e_k-\alpha\frac{L+\mu}2e_k+\alpha\frac M2\sigma_k+\beta(e_k-e_{k-1})$,
which is \eqref{eq:normrec}. For Polyak's tuning
$\alpha(L+\mu)/2=1+q^2$ and $\alpha(L-\mu)/2=2q$.
head: environment

label: eq:convexinterp
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $F_i=\psi_i+\frac12\lVert x_i\rVert^2$ and $G_i=\sigma_i+x_i$. Expanding the squares
in \eqref{eq:interpolation} shows that the two inequalities $T_{ij}\le R_{ij}$
and $T_{ji}\le R_{ji}$, for all $i,j$, are equivalent to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:convexinterp}
 F_i\ge F_j+\langle G_j,x_i-x_j\rangle+\tfrac14\lVert G_i-G_j\rVert^2\quad(i,j\in I).
\end{equation}
We first prove necessity. If $\psi\in\mathcal S$, then $F=\psi+\frac12\lVert \cdot\rVert^2$ is convex, because
$\nabla F=\nabla\psi+\mathrm{id}$ is monotone by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality
and the $1$-Lipschitz property, and $\nabla F$ is $2$-Lipschitz. The function
$F-\langle G_j,\cdot\rangle$ is convex, $2$-smooth and minimized at $x_j$; the descent
inequality at $x_i$ gives
$F_i-\langle G_j,x_i\rangle\ge F_j-\langle G_j,x_j\rangle+\frac14\lVert G_i-G_j\rVert^2$, which is
\eqref{eq:convexinterp}.

We now prove sufficiency. Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:extension}
 H(y)=\sup_{i\in I}\Bigl\{\langle x_i,y\rangle-F_i+\tfrac14\lVert y-G_i\rVert^2\Bigr\},\quad
 \psi(x)=H^*(x)-\tfrac12\lVert x\rVert^2 .
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq:convexinterp}, the $j$th term attains the supremum at $y=G_j$:
for every $i$,
$\langle x_i,G_j\rangle-F_i+\frac14\lVert G_j-G_i\rVert^2\le\langle x_j,G_j\rangle-F_j$. Hence
$H(G_j)=\langle x_j,G_j\rangle-F_j$ is finite, $H$ is proper, convex and lower
semicontinuous, and $H-\frac14\lVert \cdot\rVert^2$ is convex as a supremum of affine
functions, so $H$ is $\frac12$-strongly convex. The datum $(0,0,0)$ gives
$H(y)\ge\frac14\lVert y\rVert^2$. The $j$th quadratic touches $H$ from below at
$G_j$ and has gradient $x_j$ there, so $x_j\in\partial H(G_j)$. For every $x$,
the function $y\mapsto H(y)-\langle x,y\rangle$ is coercive and strongly convex; a
minimizing sequence is bounded, has a weakly convergent subsequence, and weak
lower semicontinuity gives a unique minimizer. Hence $H^*$ is finite and
differentiable everywhere, and $\nabla H^*$ is $2$-Lipschitz because $H$ is
$\frac12$-strongly convex. Conjugate subgradients give
$\nabla H^*(x_j)=G_j$ and $H^*(x_j)=\langle x_j,G_j\rangle-H(G_j)=F_j$. Finally
$H^*$ is convex and $2$-smooth, so the cocoercivity inequality for
$\nabla H^*$ with constant $2$ gives
$\lVert (\nabla H^*(x)-x)-(\nabla H^*(z)-z)\rVert^2\le\lVert x-z\rVert^2$. Thus
$\psi\in\mathcal S$, $\nabla\psi(x_i)=G_i-x_i=\sigma_i$ and
$\psi(x_i)=F_i-\frac12\lVert x_i\rVert^2=\psi_i$; the datum at $0$ gives $\psi(0)=0$
and $\nabla\psi(0)=0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider first one wave, $e_k=z^k$, $\sigma_k=mz^k$, $\psi_k=\mathsf he^{2kt}$, with
$\mathsf h=\frac14(C+2\operatorname{Re} m)$. For $j=0$ and a lag $n\ge1$,
\[
 T_{0n}=\mathsf h(e^{2nt}-1)-\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\bigl[m(1+z^{n})\overline{(z^{n}-1)}\bigr]
 =\tfrac C4(e^{2nt}-1)-s\,\operatorname{Im} z^{n},
\]
because $(1+z^{n})\overline{(z^{n}-1)}=|z|^{2n}-1-2i\operatorname{Im} z^{n}$; and
$R_{0n}=\frac14(1-|m|^2)|z^{n}-1|^2=\frac g4|z^{n}-1|^2$. With
$e^{2nt}-1=2e^{nt}\sinh nt$, $|z^{n}-1|^2=2e^{nt}(\cosh nt-\cos n\omega)$ and
$\operatorname{Im} z^{n}=e^{nt}\sin n\omega$,
\[
 R_{0n}\pm T_{0n}=\tfrac12e^{nt}\bigl(a_{n}\mp b_{n}\pm C\sinh nt\bigr).
\]
Replacing the indices $(0,n)$ by $(j,j+n)$ multiplies positions and
gradients by $z^j$ and values by $e^{2jt}$, hence multiplies both $R$ and $T$
by $e^{2jt}$. For the pair with the minimizer,
$T_{\star j}=\psi_j-\frac12\langle \sigma_j,e_j\rangle=(\mathsf h-\frac12\operatorname{Re} m)e^{2jt}=\frac C4e^{2jt}$
and $R_{j\star}=\frac14(1-|m|^2)e^{2jt}$, which gives the second identity in
\eqref{eq:waveslacks}. An orthogonal sum of waves with a common exponent is
realized in $L^2([0,\pi],\nu;\mathbb C)$, regarded as a real Hilbert space, by
$e_k(\omega)=e^{k(t+i\omega)}$, $\sigma_k(\omega)=m(t,\omega)e_k(\omega)$ and
the stated values. Inner products and squared norms are integrals over $\nu$
of the corresponding quantities for single waves, and the values are
prescribed by the common constant; hence \eqref{eq:waveslacks} holds with
averages. Theorem~\ref{thm:interpolation} now shows that interpolation is
equivalent to $R\pm T\ge0$ for all pairs, that is, to \eqref{eq:feasible}.
Every finite segment of this realization lies in a finite-dimensional
subspace.

label: lem:compact
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:compact}
For fixed $t$, the set of pairs $(\nu,C)$ feasible at $t$ is compact in the
product of the weak topology on probability measures on $[0,\pi]$ and the
real line. For Polyak's tuning the set of $(v,t,\nu,C)$ feasible in the sense
of \eqref{eq:VT} with $(v,t)$ in a compact set is compact, and feasibility
implies $|\sinh v|\le1$.
head: environment
name: Compactness

title: Proof
body_md:
Probability measures on the compact interval $[0,\pi]$ form a weakly compact
set. The minimizer constraint gives $|C|\le\bar g\le1$, since
$g=1-|m|^2\le1$. For each fixed lag $n$, the functions $a_n$, $b_n$
and $g$ are continuous in $(t,\omega)$, so every constraint in
\eqref{eq:feasible} is closed under weak convergence of $\nu$ and convergence
of $C$ and $t$. For Polyak's tuning the same holds in $(v,t)$, and
$0\le\bar g=1-\int c^2d\nu-\sinh^2v\le1-\sinh^2v$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
A feasible pair contradicts a strict certificate: integrating the first line
of \eqref{eq:strictcert} against $\nu$ and using the second line gives
$\sum_m(\alpha_m\ell_m+\beta_m\upsilon_m)+\gamma_+(\bar g+C)+\gamma_-(\bar g-C)
=\int\Phi_t\,d\nu\le-\varepsilon$, while the left side is nonnegative.
Conversely, suppose \eqref{eq:feasible} is infeasible at $t$. For $M'\ge1$ let
$\mathcal P_{M'}$ be the set of pairs satisfying the minimizer constraint and
the lag constraints with $m\le M'$. These are compact by
Lemma~\ref{lem:compact}, decreasing in $M'$, and their intersection is empty;
hence $\mathcal P_{M'}=\emptyset$ for some $M'$. Write this finite system as
$\int\phi_i\,d\nu+\varsigma_iC\ge0$, $i\in\mathcal I$, with continuous $\phi_i$
and real $\varsigma_i$. The set
\[
 \mathcal K=\operatorname{conv}\bigl\{(\phi_i(\omega))_{i\in\mathcal I}:\omega\in[0,\pi]\bigr\}
 +\mathbb R\,\varsigma-\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal I}
\]
is the sum of a compact convex set and a finitely generated cone, hence closed
and convex. It contains no vector with all coordinates nonnegative, since such a
vector would give a feasible pair. In particular $0\notin\mathcal K$, and the
whole orthant $\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal I}$ is disjoint from $\mathcal K$. Strict
separation of $0$ from $\mathcal K$ gives $\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal I}$ and
$\varepsilon>0$ with $\lambda\cdot k\le-\varepsilon$ for all $k\in\mathcal K$.
Because $\mathcal K$ contains $k-\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal I}$ and $k+\mathbb R\varsigma$,
$\lambda\ge0$ and $\lambda\cdot\varsigma=0$. With $\lambda$ split into the
weights $\alpha_m,\beta_m,\gamma_\pm$, these statements are
\eqref{eq:strictcert}.
head: environment

label: lem:envelope
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:envelope}
$\Gamma$ is finite and submultiplicative, the limit
$\rho_\Gamma=\lim_p\Gamma(p)^{1/p}=\inf_{p\ge1}\Gamma(p)^{1/p}$ exists,
$\rho_\Gamma\ge\rho_{\rm q}>0$, and $W_N\le\sqrt2\,\Gamma(N)$ for $N\ge0$. If
$(\nu,C)$ is feasible at $t$, then $\Gamma(p)\ge e^{pt}$ for all $p$.
head: environment
name: Growth envelope

title: Proof
body_md:
The minimizer inequality gives $\lVert \sigma_k\rVert\le\lVert e_k\rVert$, hence
$\lVert e_{k+1}\rVert\le(|A|+B)\lVert e_k\rVert+\beta\lVert e_{k-1}\rVert$, and componentwise
$\binom{\lVert e_{k+p-1}\rVert}{\lVert e_{k+p}\rVert}\le\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\\beta&|A|+B\end{pmatrix}^p\binom{\lVert e_{k-1}\rVert}{\lVert e_k\rVert}$;
so $\Gamma(p)$ is finite. If $S_{k+p}=0$, the minimizer inequality forces
$\sigma_{k+p}=0$ and then $S_l=0$ for all $l\ge k+p$; otherwise
$\lVert S_{k+p+r}\rVert/\lVert S_k\rVert=(\lVert S_{k+p+r}\rVert/\lVert S_{k+p}\rVert)(\lVert S_{k+p}\rVert/\lVert S_k\rVert)$,
and restricting a segment to consecutive indices gives a segment. Thus
$\Gamma(p+r)\le\Gamma(p)\Gamma(r)$, and Fekete's lemma gives the limit. The
quadratic functions $\frac\lambda2\lVert \cdot\rVert^2$, $\lambda\in[\mu,L]$, give
segments growing like $\rho_{\rm q}^p$, and $\rho_{\rm q}>0$: the two characteristic roots
for the curvature $\lambda$ have product $\beta$, and for $\beta=0$ they are $0$
and $1-\alpha\lambda$, which is nonzero for every $\lambda\in[\mu,L]$ except at
most one. For a trajectory of \eqref{eq:hb}, prepending
$e_{-1}=e_0$ gives a segment with $\lVert S_0\rVert=\sqrt2\lVert e_0\rVert$, so
$W_N\le\sqrt2\Gamma(N)$. Finally, by Lemma~\ref{lem:spectralinterp} a feasible
spectrum yields segments of every length with $\lVert S_k\rVert^2=e^{2kt}(1+e^{-2t})$.
head: environment

label: lem:energy
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Energy estimate

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $I^\pm_{k,n}=R_{k,k+n}\pm T_{k,k+n}$ and $I^\pm_{k\star}=R_{k\star}\pm T_{\star k}$, and
consider the nonnegative combination
\[
 Z_k=\sum_{n\le M'}2e^{-nt}\bigl(\alpha_nI^+_{k,n}+\beta_nI^-_{k,n}\bigr)
 +4\gamma_+I^+_{k\star}+4\gamma_-I^-_{k\star}\ \ge0 .
\]
Put $f_k=e^{-kt}e_k$, $h_k=e^{-2kt}\psi_k$, and substitute
$\sigma_k=(e_{k+1}-Ae_k+\beta e_{k-1})/B$. Then
$e^{-2kt}Z_k=\mathcal Q_k(f)+\mathcal H_k(h)$, where $\mathcal Q_k$ is a
translation-invariant quadratic form in $f_{k-1},\dots,f_{k+M'+1}$ and
\[
 \mathcal H_k(h)=\sum_n2e^{-nt}(\alpha_n-\beta_n)\bigl(e^{2nt}h_{k+n}-h_k\bigr)+4(\gamma_+-\gamma_-)h_k .
\]
In $\sum_{k=i}^j\mathcal H_k(h)$ the coefficient of every $h_l$ with
$i+M'\le l\le j$ is $4\{\sum_n(\alpha_n-\beta_n)\sinh nt+\gamma_+-\gamma_-\}=0$.
The remaining terms involve $h_l$ with $l$ in the windows around $i$ and $j$.
The minimizer inequality gives $|T_{\star l}|\le R_{l\star}$, that is,
$|\psi_l-\frac12\langle \sigma_l,e_l\rangle|\le\frac14(\lVert e_l\rVert^2-\lVert \sigma_l\rVert^2)$,
whence $|\psi_l|\le\frac12\lVert e_l\rVert^2$; so these terms are bounded by
$K_h(E_i+E_j)$.

Write $\mathcal Q_k(f)=\sum_{a,b}q_{ab}\langle f_{k+a},f_{k+b}\rangle$ with a symmetric
coefficient matrix. On the complex exponential $f_l=e^{il\omega}$, which
corresponds to the wave $e_l=z^l$, $\sigma_l=mz^l$, the value is
$\sum_{a,b}q_{ab}\cos((b-a)\omega)=\Phi_t(\omega)$: by \eqref{eq:waveslacks}
the combination $Z_k$ of the wave data equals
$e^{2kt}\{\sum_n(\alpha_n(a_n-b_n+C\sinh nt)+\beta_n(a_n+b_n-C\sinh nt))
+\gamma_+(g+C)+\gamma_-(g-C)\}$, and the terms with $C$ are exactly the
function-value terms, which cancel. Parseval's identity gives, for every
finitely supported sequence $F$ in a Hilbert space,
\[
 \sum_k\mathcal Q_k(F)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\Phi_t(|\theta|)\,\lVert \widehat F(\theta)\rVert^2d\theta
 \le-\varepsilon\sum_k\lVert F_k\rVert^2 .
\]
Apply this to $F=f\mathbf 1_{[i-1,j+M'+1]}$. The terms $\mathcal Q_k(F)$ with
$k\notin[i,j]$, and the differences $\mathcal Q_k(F)-\mathcal Q_k(f)$ for
$k\in[i,j]$, involve only boundary windows, and
$|\langle f_a,f_b\rangle|\le\frac12(\mathsf b_a+\mathsf b_b)$ bounds them by $K_1(E_i+E_j)$. Since
$Z_k\ge0$,
$\varepsilon\sum_{k=i}^j\mathsf b_k\le(K_1+K_h)(E_i+E_j)$.

label: lem:plateau
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:plateau}
There is no strict certificate at $t=\log\rho_\Gamma$.
head: environment
name: No strict certificate at the growth exponent

label: eq:forward
title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose there is one and put $r=\rho_\Gamma$,
$\gamma(p)=\Gamma(p)r^{-p}$, $\bar\gamma(p)=\max_{0\le l\le p}\gamma(l)$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:envelope}, $\gamma(p)\ge1$ and $\bar\gamma(p)^{1/p}\to1$. For
$l\ge k\ge1$, $\lVert e_l\rVert\le\lVert S_l\rVert\le\Gamma(l-k)\lVert S_k\rVert$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:forward}
 \mathsf b_l\le c_r\gamma(l-k)^2(\mathsf b_{k-1}+\mathsf b_k),\quad c_r=\max(1,r^{-2}).
\end{equation}
Let $K,w$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:energy}, $\theta=1+1/(2K)$, $a=2w+1$, and
choose an integer $p_0$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:choosep}
 \theta^{p_0}>1+p_0ac_r\bar\gamma(p_0a+w)^2,
\end{equation}
which is possible by subexponential growth of $\bar\gamma$. Write $L'=p_0a$.

First, if $i\ge w$, $j\ge i+2w$ and $j\le n-L'$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:shortgrowth}
 B_i(j):=\sum_{k=i}^j\mathsf b_k\le2KE_i .
\end{equation}
Otherwise \eqref{eq:energy} gives $E_l>B_i(l)/(2K)$ for $j\le l\le n-w$. Since
$E_l=B_i(l+w)-B_i(l-w-1)$, this gives $B_i(l+w)\ge\theta B_i(l-w-1)$, and
iterating at $l=j+w+1+pa$, $0\le p<p_0$, yields $B_i(j+L')\ge\theta^{p_0}B_i(j)$.
On the other hand \eqref{eq:forward} with $k=j-w$ gives
$B_i(j+L')\le B_i(j)\{1+L'c_r\bar\gamma(L'+w)^2\}$, which contradicts
\eqref{eq:choosep}.

Second, put $n'=n-L'$ and $\mathsf T_i=\sum_{k=i}^{n'}\mathsf b_k$. For $w\le i\le n'-2w$,
\eqref{eq:shortgrowth} gives $\mathsf T_i\le2KE_i\le2K(\mathsf T_{i-w}-\mathsf T_{i+w+1})$, hence
$\mathsf T_{i+w+1}\le\theta^{-1}\mathsf T_{i-w}$, and $\mathsf T_{pa}\le\theta^{-p}\mathsf T_0$ as long as the
windows fit. Moreover $\mathsf T_0\le(1+2K)E_w\le C_w\lVert S_1\rVert^2$, with $C_w$
depending only on $\Gamma(l)$, $l\le2w$, and $r$. The last such window ends at
distance at most $L'+4w+2$ from $n$; applying \eqref{eq:forward} over these
finitely many steps gives $\lVert S_n\rVert^2\le Cr^{2n}\theta^{-n/a}\lVert S_1\rVert^2$ with
$C$ independent of the segment and of $n$. Hence
$\rho_\Gamma\le r\theta^{-1/(2a)}<r$, a contradiction.

body_md:
Suppose strict certificates exist at every $t\ge t_0$. If $\rho_\Gamma\ge e^{t_0}$,
there is a strict certificate at $t=\log\rho_\Gamma\ge t_0$, which contradicts

label: lem:startup
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:startup}
Let $(\nu,C)$ be feasible at $t$, with atoms $\omega_1,\dots,\omega_r$ and
weights $\nu_j>0$, and assume $|C|<\bar g$ if $t>0$. Then there are
$f\in\mathcal F_{\mu,L}(\mathbb R^{2r+1})$ and $x_0$ with $x_{-1}=x_0$ such that
$\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert\ge c\,e^{kt}\lVert x_0-x^\star\rVert$ for all $k\ge0$, with $c>0$
independent of $k$. The trajectory is the orthogonal sum of the $r$ waves in
$2r$ coordinates and a sequence $y_k\to0$ in the last coordinate.
head: environment
name: One-coordinate initialization

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $z_j=e^{t+i\omega_j}$ and $m_j=m(t,\omega_j)$. Choose
$\tau\in(-1,1)$ and let $p_k$ be defined by $p_{-1}=p_0=1$ and
$p_{k+1}=(A+B\tau)p_k-\beta p_{k-1}$. By \eqref{eq:Abound},
$|A+B\tau|<1+\beta$, so the roots of $z^2-(A+B\tau)z+\beta$ lie in the open
unit disk and $p_k\to0$. By induction, $p_k$ is a polynomial of degree $k$ in
$\tau$ with leading coefficient $B^k$; we choose $\tau$ outside the
countable set where some $p_k=1$ with $k\ge1$. Then
$\delta_0:=\inf_{k\ge1}(1-p_k)^2>0$, because $p_k\to0$.

In $\mathbb C^r\oplus\mathbb R\cong\mathbb R^{2r+1}$ prescribe, for a parameter $Y>0$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 e_0=\bigl((\sqrt{\nu_j})_j,Y\bigr),\quad
 \sigma_0=\Bigl(\Bigl(\sqrt{\nu_j}\,\frac{z_j-A+\beta}{B}\Bigr)_j,\tau Y\Bigr),\quad
 \psi_0=\tfrac12\langle \sigma_0,e_0\rangle,\\
 e_k=\bigl((\sqrt{\nu_j}z_j^k)_j,p_kY\bigr),\quad
 \sigma_k=\bigl((\sqrt{\nu_j}m_jz_j^k)_j,\tau p_kY\bigr)\quad(k\ge1),\\
 \psi_k=\tfrac14\Bigl(C+2\sum_j\nu_j\operatorname{Re} m_j\Bigr)e^{2kt}+\tfrac\tau2p_k^2Y^2\quad(k\ge1).
 \end{gathered}
\]
The recurrence \eqref{eq:normrec} with $e_{-1}=e_0$ holds at $k=0$ by the
choice of $\sigma_0$, because $e_1=(A-\beta)e_0+B\sigma_0$; at $k\ge1$ it holds in
the mode coordinates by $Bm_jz_j=z_j^2-Az_j+\beta$ and in the last
coordinate by the recursion for $p_k$.

We verify \eqref{eq:interpolation}. The data split into the mode coordinates
and the last coordinate, and $R$ and $T$ add over orthogonal components. The
last coordinate carries the data of the quadratic $\frac\tau2y^2$, for which
$T=0$ and $R=\frac14(1-\tau^2)(y_i-y_j)^2$ for every pair. For pairs of indices
$i,j\ge1$ and for the pairs $(\star,k)$, $k\ge1$, the mode part is the
stationary data of Lemma~\ref{lem:spectralinterp}, which satisfy the
inequalities because $(\nu,C)$ is feasible. For the pair $(\star,0)$,
$T_{\star0}=\psi_0-\frac12\langle \sigma_0,e_0\rangle=0$ and
$R_{0\star}=\frac14(1+Y^2-\lVert \sigma_0\rVert^2)\ge\frac14\bigl(1+(1-\tau^2)Y^2-\sum_j\nu_j|(z_j-A+\beta)/B|^2\bigr)$,
which is nonnegative for $Y$ large. For the pairs $(0,k)$, $k\ge1$, the mode
part of $R_{0k}\pm T_{0k}$ does not depend on $Y$, and the last coordinate adds
$\frac14(1-\tau^2)Y^2(1-p_k)^2\ge\frac14(1-\tau^2)\delta_0Y^2$. If $t\le0$, the
mode parts are bounded uniformly in $k$, since all mode data are bounded. If
$t>0$, the mode part differs from the stationary value
$\frac12e^{kt}(\bar a_k\mp\bar b_k\pm C\sinh kt)$ of \eqref{eq:waveslacks} by at most
$B_1e^{kt}+B_2$, because $\sigma_0$ and $\psi_0$ differ from the stationary data
by a fixed vector and a fixed number. Since
$|\bar a_k\mp\bar b_k-\bar g\cosh kt|\le\int(|g|+2|s|)\,d\nu=:B_3$ and $\cosh kt\ge e^{kt}/2$,
the stationary value is at least $\frac14(\bar g-|C|)e^{2kt}-\frac12B_3e^{kt}$.
Hence the mode part is negative for at most finitely many $k$. In both cases a sufficiently large $Y$ makes all
inequalities hold. Theorem~\ref{thm:interpolation} gives $\psi\in\mathcal S$
interpolating all data, Lemma~\ref{lem:normalization} gives $f\in\mathcal F_{\mu,L}(\mathbb R^{2r+1})$,
and the iterates of \eqref{eq:hb} from $x_0=x^\star+e_0$ are
$x_k=x^\star+e_k$. Finally $\lVert e_k\rVert\ge e^{kt}$ and
$\lVert e_0\rVert=\sqrt{1+Y^2}$.

label: lem:vmono
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Symmetries and monotonicity in the twist

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) $a_m$ and $g$ are even in $t$, $b_m$ does not depend on $t$, and
$\sinh mt$ is odd. (ii) $a_m$ and $g$ are even in $u=\sinh v$ and $b_m$ is odd.
(iii) With $u'=\sinh v'=\theta u$, $b_m(v')=\theta b_m(v)$ and
\[
 a_m(v')=a_m(v)+(u^2-u'^2)\bigl(T_m(G)-T_m(c)\bigr)\ge a_m(v),
\]
because $T_m(G)\ge1\ge T_m(c)$. Hence
$\ell_m(v')=\theta\ell_m(v)+(1-\theta)\bar a_m(v)+(\bar a_m(v')-\bar a_m(v))$, and
$\bar a_m(v)=\frac12(\ell_m+\upsilon_m)\ge0$; the same holds for $\upsilon_m$. The
minimizer slack satisfies $\bar g(v')\ge\bar g(v)\ge|C|\ge\theta|C|$. The
consequences follow from (ii), (iii), closedness, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:compact}.

label: lem:finiteatoms
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:finiteatoms}
For Polyak's tuning let $T=T(q)\ne0$ and $v=T-\log q$. Every optimal pair
$(\nu,C)$ at $(v,T)$ has $\nu$ finitely supported in $(-1,1)$ and
$|C|<\bar g$, and only finitely many lag constraints are active.
head: environment
name: Finite support and inactive tails

title: Proof
body_md:
Divide the lag functions $a_m\mp b_m$ by $U_{m-1}(\cosh t)$, so that $C$ enters
every normalized lag constraint with the coefficient $\pm\sinh t$, and represent
the minimizer constraints, multiplied by $\sinh|t|$, as the limits $m=\infty$:
for $t\ne0$ the normalized lag functions converge uniformly on $[-1,1]$, as
$m\to\infty$, to $g\sinh|t|$. For $t>T$ the points $(t-\log q,t)$ are infeasible
by the definition of $T(q)$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:spectralgeneral}(a) gives
strict certificates. Normalized to total weight one, the certificates at a
sequence $t_n\downarrow T$ have a weakly convergent subsequence on the compact
index set $\{\mathsf L_m,\mathsf U_m:m\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}\}$. The limit is a
nonpositive symbol $\Phi_T$, with equal total lower and upper weight, and
complementary slackness places every optimal measure in the zero set of
$\Phi_T$.

In the complex strip $|\operatorname{Im}\omega|<|T|$ the trigonometric parts of the
normalized lag functions decay geometrically in $m$, so $\Phi_T$ is analytic
there. At $c=\pm1$ every normalized lag functional is at most
$-\sinh^2v\,\sinh|T|\tanh(|T|/2)<0$, so $\Phi_T$ is not identically zero; it has
finitely many zeros in $[-1,1]$, all interior. Thus $\nu$ is finitely supported
in $(-1,1)$.

Suppose $|C|=\bar g$. Part (i) of Lemma~\ref{lem:vmono} maps $(T,C)$ to
$(-T,-C)$, so we may take $T>0$. Put $u=\sinh v$ and
$z_j=-\nu_j(g_j+2iu\sin\omega_j)$, so that
\[
 f(m):=\operatorname{Re}\sum_jz_je^{im\omega_j}=\sum_j\nu_j\{2u\sin\omega_j\sin m\omega_j-g_j\cos m\omega_j\}.
\]
If $C=\bar g$, the upper constraints give $f(m)\ge-\bar ge^{-mT}$; if
$C=-\bar g$, the lower constraints give the same bound for the function
obtained by negating the sine term, that is, with $z_j$ replaced by its
conjugate, and the argument below applies verbatim. The atoms are distinct
points of $(0,\pi)$, so the Ces\`aro means satisfy
$N^{-1}\sum_{m\le N}f(m)\to0$ and
$N^{-1}\sum_{m\le N}f(m)^2\to\frac12\sum_j|z_j|^2$. Here
$|z_j|^2=\nu_j^2(g_j^2+4u^2\sin^2\omega_j)>0$: for $u\ne0$ the second term is
positive, and for $u=0$ one has $g_j=\sin^2\omega_j>0$. The lower bound makes
the Ces\`aro mean of the negative part $f^-$ tend to zero; together with
$N^{-1}\sum f(m)\to0$, the means of $|f|$ tend to zero, and since $f$ is
bounded the means of $f^2$ tend to zero, a contradiction. Hence
$|C|<\bar g$.

Finally, with $\eta=\bar g-|C|>0$ every raw lag slack is at least
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tail}
 \eta\cosh(m|T|)-(1+u)^2,
\end{equation}
since $|g(c)|\le1+u^2$ and $|2u\sin\omega\sin m\omega|\le2u$; so only finitely
many lags are active.
head: environment

label: eq:freeidentity
title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{lem:vmono} gives the description of the feasible $v$ and the
bound on $V$. Lemma~\ref{lem:compact} shows that the maximum defining $T(q)$
is attained; the spiral of Proposition~\ref{prop:spiral} is feasible, so
the set is nonempty. For $t>T(q)$, $|t-\log q|>V(t)$, so the actual point
$(t-\log q,t)$ is infeasible and a strict certificate exists by
Theorem~\ref{thm:spectralgeneral}(a); Theorem~\ref{thm:spectralgeneral}(b)
gives $\rho_\Gamma<e^{t_0}$ and $\rho_{\rm HB}<e^{t_0}$ for every $t_0>T(q)$, hence
$\rho_{\rm HB}\le e^{T(q)}$; together with Lemma~\ref{lem:envelope},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:freeidentity}
 \rho_\Gamma=e^{T(q)} .
\end{equation}
At $t=T(q)$
the actual point is feasible. If $T(q)\ne0$, Lemma~\ref{lem:finiteatoms} gives
a finitely supported optimal spectrum with $|C|<\bar g$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:startup} gives $\rho_{\rm HB}\ge e^{T(q)}$. If $T(q)=0$, then
$q=\varphi^{-1}$ by Propositions~\ref{prop:strip} and~\ref{prop:spiral}, and the three-cycle of
Proposition~\ref{prop:spiral} is a one-atom feasible spectrum at $t=0$, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:startup} applies again. The remaining assertions are
Lemma~\ref{lem:finiteatoms}.

label: lem:spiralids
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:spiralids}
On the data \eqref{eq:spiralsimple}, for every $m\ge1$,
$\ell_m=gE_{m+1}(t)/G$ and $\upsilon_m=gE_{m-1}(t)/G$, where

head: environment
name: Lag identities on the spiral

title: Proof
body_md:
From \eqref{eq:spiralsimple}, $\sin\omega=\sqrt{4G^2-1}/(2G)$ and
$2u(1-c^2)/g=(4G^2-1)/(2G)$, so that
$b_m/g=2u(1-c^2)U_{m-1}(c)/g=\sqrt{4G^2-1}\,\sin m\omega$. Hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{\ell_m}g&=\cosh mt+\tanh t\sinh mt-\cos m\omega-\sqrt{4G^2-1}\sin m\omega,\\
 \frac{\upsilon_m}g&=\cosh mt-\tanh t\sinh mt-\cos m\omega+\sqrt{4G^2-1}\sin m\omega .
 \end{aligned}
\]
The addition formulas give $\cosh(m\pm1)t/G=\cosh mt\pm\tanh t\sinh mt$ and
$2G\cos(m\pm1)\omega=2G\cos m\omega\cos\omega\mp2G\sin m\omega\sin\omega
=-\cos m\omega\mp\sqrt{4G^2-1}\sin m\omega$. Substituting these formulas,
with the upper signs into the first displayed line and the lower signs into
the second, gives $\ell_m/g=\{\cosh(m+1)t+2G^2\cos(m+1)\omega\}/G=E_{m+1}/G$ and
$\upsilon_m/g=\{\cosh(m-1)t+2G^2\cos(m-1)\omega\}/G=E_{m-1}/G$. Finally $E_1=G+2G^2c=0$ and
$E_2=2G^2-1+2G^2(2c^2-1)=0$.
head: environment

label: lem:spiralkernel
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:spiralkernel}
Let $s=G^2-1$ and $F_n=G^{n-2}E_n$. For every $n\ge3$, $F_n$ is a polynomial
in $s$ with nonnegative coefficients, $F_n(0)=3$ if $3\mid n$ and $F_n(0)=0$
otherwise, and $F_n(s)>0$ for $s>0$. In particular $E_n(t)>0$ for $n\ge3$ and
$t\ne0$.
head: environment
name: Positivity of the spiral kernel

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $X=G^2=1+s$. The generating function
$\sum_{n\ge0}T_n(x)r^n=(1-xr)/(1-2xr+r^2)$, applied with $x=G$ and $x=-1/(2G)$
and the variable $Gr$, gives
\[
 \sum_{n\ge0}F_nr^n=\frac{1-Xr}{X(1-2Xr+Xr^2)}+\frac{2+r}{1+r+Xr^2} .
\]
Since $F_1=F_2=0$ and $F_0=(1+2X)/X$, a direct computation gives
\[
 \sum_{n\ge3}F_nr^n=\frac{(2X+1)\,r^3\,(2X-1-Xr)}{(1+r+Xr^2)(1-2Xr+Xr^2)}
 =\frac{(2s+3)\,r^3\,\{(1-r)+s(2-r)\}}{D},
\]
where $D=(1+r+Xr^2)(1-2Xr+Xr^2)=D_0-sD_1-s^2D_2$ with
\[
 D_0=(1-r)(1-r^3),\quad D_1=r(2+3r^2-2r^3),\quad D_2=r^3(2-r).
\]
As formal power series in $r$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q[s]$,
\[
 \frac{(1-r)+s(2-r)}{D}=\sum_{k\ge0}\Bigl(s\frac{D_1}{1-r}+s^2\frac{D_2}{1-r}\Bigr)^k
 \frac1{(1-r^3)^{k+1}}\Bigl(1+s\frac{2-r}{1-r}\Bigr),
\]
and the series converges coefficientwise because $D_1$ and $D_2$ have no
constant term. Each factor has nonnegative coefficients:
$D_1/(1-r)=2r+2r^2+5r^3+3\sum_{j\ge4}r^j$,
$D_2/(1-r)=2r^3+\sum_{j\ge4}r^j$, $(2-r)/(1-r)=2+\sum_{j\ge1}r^j$, and
$1/(1-r^3)=\sum_jr^{3j}$. Hence every $F_n$, $n\ge3$, has nonnegative
coefficients in $s$. The terms with $k\ge1$ are divisible by $s$. The term
$k=0$ contributes to $F_n$ the polynomial $(2s+3)\{[3\mid n]+s\,c_n\}$, where
$c_n$ is the coefficient of $r^{n-3}$ in $(2-r)/((1-r)(1-r^3))$, and $c_n\ge1$.
This gives the value at $s=0$ and strict positivity for $s>0$. Finally
$s=\sinh^2t$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemmas~\ref{lem:spiralids} and~\ref{lem:spiralkernel},
$\ell_1=\upsilon_2=\upsilon_3=0$, $\upsilon_1=g(1+2G^2)/G>0$, and all other
raw slacks are positive multiples of $E_n$, $n\ge3$, hence positive for
$t\ne0$. Moreover $g>0$ and $|C|=g|\tanh t|<\bar g=g$. This is
\eqref{eq:En} and the feasibility. On the spiral,
$1-\frac1{2G}=(\varrho^2-\varrho+1)/(\varrho^2+1)$ with $\varrho=e^t$, and
$\sinh(t-\log q)=\frac12(\varrho/q-q/\varrho)$; equating the two and multiplying
by $2q\varrho(\varrho^2+1)$ gives $F(\varrho,q)=0$.

label: lem:tailsharp
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Amplitude identity and tail bound

title: Proof
body_md:
With $k=1-c^2$, $(k-u^2)^2+4u^2k=(k+u^2)^2$. For one frequency,
$a_m\mp b_m=g\cosh mt-\{g\cos m\omega\pm2u\sin\omega\sin m\omega\}$, and by the
identity and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality the braces are at most $1-c^2+u^2$
in absolute value. Integrating gives
$\bar a_m\mp\bar b_m\ge\bar g\cosh mt-(\bar g+2u^2)$, and
$|C\sinh mt|\le|C|\cosh mt$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $a_1-b_1=g(G-c)-2u(1-c^2)$ and $U_0=1$, and since $\sum_{m\in J}w_m=1$,
\[
 \Phi(c)=g\Bigl\{(G-c)+\sum_mw_m\frac{T_m(G)-T_m(c)}{U_{m-1}(G)}\Bigr\}
 -2u(1-c^2)\sum_mw_m\frac{U_{m-1}(G)-U_{m-1}(c)}{U_{m-1}(G)} .
\]
This is \eqref{eq:alphabeta} with
\[
 \alpha_J=1+\sum_{m\in J}w_m\frac{T_m(G)-T_m(c)}{(G-c)U_{m-1}(G)},\quad
 \beta_J=\sum_{m\in J}w_m\frac{U_{m-1}(G)-U_{m-1}(c)}{(G-c)U_{m-1}(G)},
\]
where the quotients by $G-c$ are polynomials in $(G,c)$. For $G\ge1\ge c$,
$T_m(G)\ge1\ge T_m(c)$ and $U_{m-1}(G)\ge m\ge U_{m-1}(c)$, so $\alpha_J\ge1$
and $\beta_J\ge0$, and both are independent of $u$. Hence $Q=-\Phi/(G-c)$ is a polynomial
and, for $u'\ge u\ge0$,
$\Phi_{G,u'}-\Phi_{G,u}=-(G-c)\{(u'^2-u^2)\alpha_J+2(u'-u)(1-c^2)\beta_J\}
\le-(G-c)(u'^2-u^2)$.
head: environment

label: prop:spiralsub
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: The spiral outside its regime

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f=(\ell_1,\upsilon_2,\upsilon_3)$ be the active raw slacks of the spiral as
functions of $(\omega,C,t)$, with $v=t-\log q$, and let $\mathsf J=[\partial_\omega f,\partial_Cf]$
and $b=\partial_tf$ at the spiral point. The vector
$y=(1,W/U_1(G),(1-W)/U_2(G))$ satisfies $y^{\mathsf T}\partial_Cf=0$ because
$\sinh mt=U_{m-1}(G)\sinh t$, and $y^{\mathsf T}\partial_\omega f=0$ because the zero
of \eqref{eq:spiralcertificate} at $c=-1/(2G)$ is double. Moreover
\[
 \partial_\omega\Bigl(\frac{\upsilon_2}{U_1(G)}-\frac{\upsilon_3}{U_2(G)}\Bigr)
 =-\sin\omega\,\frac{(4G+1)(2G^2+1)}{2G^3(2G+1)}\ne0,
\]
so $\partial_\omega f$ is not a multiple of $\partial_Cf$, $\mathsf J$ has rank two,
and its image is $y^\perp$.

If $G>G_W$, then $W<0$ and $y$ has entries of both signs. Choose a vector
$r$ with positive entries and $y^{\mathsf T}r=y^{\mathsf T}b$, and solve
$\mathsf J\Delta=r-b$. At the exponent $t_{\rm sp}+\tau$ and the data
$(\omega,C)+\tau\Delta$, the three active slacks equal $\tau r+O(\tau^2)$, hence
are positive for small $\tau>0$.

If $1<G<G_1$, then $0<W<1$, $y$ has positive entries, and
\eqref{eq:spiralcertificate} is positive at $c_0=(2G-1)/(4G)$. Replace $\nu$ by
$(1-\epsilon\tau)\delta_c+\epsilon\tau\delta_{c_0}$. The first-order change $d_0$ of
the active slacks satisfies $y^{\mathsf T}d_0=\Phi(c_0)-\Phi(c)=\Phi(c_0)>0$.
Choose $\epsilon$ with $y^{\mathsf T}(b+\epsilon d_0)>0$, a positive vector $r$ with
$y^{\mathsf T}r=y^{\mathsf T}(b+\epsilon d_0)$, and solve
$\mathsf J\Delta=r-b-\epsilon d_0$; again the active slacks become positive for small
$\tau>0$.

In both cases the other fixed-lag slacks and the minimizer slack are positive
at the spiral by Lemma~\ref{lem:spiralkernel} and $|C|<g$, and they remain
positive under small perturbations. By \eqref{eq:tailsharp}, all lags with
$(\bar g-|C|)\cosh mt>2(\bar g+2u^2)$ are positive uniformly on a neighborhood of
the spiral point, since $t_{\rm sp}\ne0$. Hence the perturbed spectrum is feasible
at $(t-\log q,t)$ with $t=t_{\rm sp}+\tau$, and $T(q)>t_{\rm sp}$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:spectral} gives $\rho_{\rm HB}>\rho_{\rm sp}$.
head: environment

label: prop:strip
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Threshold strip

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:vmono}(ii) we may assume $v\ge0$, so $u\ge0$. Let $\varrho=e^{|t|}$.
If $t\ge0$, add $\sinh t$ times $\bar g-C\ge0$ to $\ell_1\ge0$; if $t<0$, add
$|\sinh t|$ times $\bar g+C\ge0$. Since $G+\sinh|t|=\varrho$, in both cases
\[
 \int h_\varrho\,d\nu\ge0,\quad h_\varrho(c)=(1-c^2-u^2)(\varrho-c)-2u(1-c^2).
\]
The function $h_\varrho$ decreases in $u\ge0$, because
$\partial_uh_\varrho=-2u(\varrho-c)-2(1-c^2)\le0$. Let $u_\varrho=\sinh(|t|+\log\varphi)$ and put
$c=1-2\mathsf x$, $\varrho=1+\mathsf y$. Then
\[
 -4\varphi^2\varrho^2\,h_\varrho(c)\big|_{u=u_\varrho}=A_3\mathsf x^3+A_2\mathsf x^2+A_1\mathsf x+A_0,
\]
with $A_3=16(3+\sqrt5)(1+\mathsf y)^2$,
\[
 A_0=\tfrac{\mathsf y}2\bigl\{(7+3\sqrt5)\mathsf y^4+(28+12\sqrt5)\mathsf y^3+(36+16\sqrt5)\mathsf y^2+(16+8\sqrt5)\mathsf y+3+\sqrt5\bigr\},
\]
and the coefficients of $4A_1A_3-A_2^2$, in increasing powers of $\mathsf y$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 0,\quad 5888+2816\sqrt5,\quad 24448+11648\sqrt5,\quad 39936+18944\sqrt5,\\
 32000+15104\sqrt5,\quad 12544+5888\sqrt5,\quad 1920+896\sqrt5 .
 \end{gathered}
\]
Writing the cubic as
$A_3\mathsf x\bigl(\mathsf x+\frac{A_2}{2A_3}\bigr)^2+\frac{4A_1A_3-A_2^2}{4A_3}\mathsf x+A_0$ shows that it is
nonnegative for $\mathsf x\in[0,1]$ and $\mathsf y\ge0$, and positive when $\mathsf y>0$. Hence for
$t\ne0$ and $u\ge u_\varrho$, $h_\varrho<0$ on $[-1,1]$, so $\int h_\varrho\,d\nu<0$, which is
impossible; thus $u<u_\varrho$, which is \eqref{eq:thresholdstrip} with strict
inequality. At $t=0$ and $u=\frac12$ the identity reduces to
$h_1(c)=-(1-c)(c+\frac12)^2$. For $u>\frac12$, $h_1<0$ on $[-1,1)$ and
$h_1(1)=0$, so $\int h_1\,d\nu\ge0$ forces $\nu=\delta_1$, which violates
$\bar g\ge0$ because $g(1)=-u^2$. Finally, for $\nu=\delta_{-1/2}$, $C=0$, $t=0$
and $u=\frac12$, Lemma~\ref{lem:spiralids} applies with $G=1$: all raw slacks
are $gE_n$ with $g=\frac12$ and $E_n=1+2\cos(2\pi n/3)\in\{0,3\}$, and
$|C|=0<\bar g$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $q<\varphi^{-1}$, then $\log q<-\log\varphi$, and every $t\ge0$ has
$t-\log q>t+\log\varphi$, so by Proposition~\ref{prop:strip} the actual point
$(t-\log q,t)$ is infeasible. Hence $T(q)<0$. At $t=T(q)$,
$v=T-\log q\le|T|+\log\varphi=-T+\log\varphi$ gives $T\le\frac12\log(\varphi q)$,
so $\rho_{\rm HB}=e^{T(q)}\le\sqrt{\varphi q}<1$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:spectral}. If
$q=\varphi^{-1}$, the three-cycle is feasible at the actual point
$(\log\varphi,0)$, and for $t>0$ the actual point has $v=t+\log\varphi$, which
Proposition~\ref{prop:strip} excludes; thus $T(q)=0$ and $\rho_{\rm HB}=1$. If
$q>\varphi^{-1}$, then $\rho_{\rm sp}>1$, and the spiral is feasible at the actual point
with $t=\log\rho_{\rm sp}>0$, so $\rho_{\rm HB}\ge\rho_{\rm sp}>1$. The trajectory statements are the case
$\rho_{\rm sp}\ge1$ of \eqref{eq:spirallower}, proved in Appendix~\ref{app:finite}: at
$\kappa_c$ the spiral is the three-cycle, and the realized trajectory
consists of the cycle and a coordinate $2(-q^2)^{\lceil k/2\rceil}\to0$.

label: prop:p1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:p1}
The continued branch of $P_1$ on $0<z\le z_W=\sqrt3-1=G_W^{-1}$ consists of
feasible and optimal spectra: $\nu=\delta_{c_1}$ with $-z/2\le c_1<0$,
$\eta=g-|C|\ge z^3/4$, $Q_1(c)=(c-c_1)^2(q_2c^2+q_1c+q_0)$ with $q_2=z^2$ and
$q_0-|q_1|>0$, and all lag slacks nonnegative. At $z_W$ the branch equals the
spiral, $\mathcal A=0$, $\mathcal B=-1/(2z_W)$. Moreover $u$ increases in $G$,
$\frac12<u<1$, and $|V'|<1$ along the branch.
head: environment
name: The family $P_1$

label: eq:p1slackpoly
title: Proof
body_md:
The interval checks on every slab give $\mathcal B<0$, $g/z>\frac12$,
$u<1$, $u_z<0$, $(\frac12+z\mathcal B)'<0$, the factorization of $Q_1$ with
$q_0-|q_1|>0$, and $u_z^2z^2(1-z^2)<1+u^2$. Since $\frac12+z_W\mathcal B(z_W)=0$,
the monotonicity gives $-z/2\le c_1<0$ on $0<z\le z_W$; likewise $u_z<0$ and
$u(z_W)=1-z_W/2>\frac12$ give $\frac12<u<1$ there. At $z_W$ exact
substitution checks both equations, and interval inclusion identifies the
exact point with the continued branch. Put
$\mathsf D=2+zc_1+z^2(c_1^2-1)$ and $\mathsf E=1+zc_1+z^2(2c_1^2-1)$. The active equation gives
$g=2uz(1-c_1^2)(1+zc_1)/\mathsf D$ and $d=2u(1-c_1^2)\mathsf E/\mathsf D$. For $-z/2\le c_1\le0$ and
$0<z\le\frac34$, $\mathsf E>0$ and $zd/g=1-z^2(1-2c_1^2)/(1+zc_1)\le1-z^2$. Hence
$|C|\le g\sqrt{1-z^2}$ and $\eta\ge gz^2/2\ge z^3/4$. After multiplication by
positive factors, each finite-lag raw slack becomes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p1slackpoly}
 z^{m-1}\bigl\{z(1+zc_1)\bigl[T_m(1/z)-T_m(c_1)\bigr]\pm\mathsf DU_{m-1}(c_1)\mp\mathsf EU_{m-1}(1/z)\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
The lower sign vanishes identically for $m=1$ and the upper sign for $m=3$.
The upper expression for $m=2$ equals $-2z(2c_1+z)(c_1z-1)\ge0$. For
$1\le m\le12$, excluding these cases, substitute $c_1=-\theta z/2$, $0\le\theta\le1$,
and remove the factor $z^2$ from the upper slacks with $m\ge4$; all tensor
Bernstein coefficients on $[0,\frac34]\times[0,1]$ are positive. For $m\ge13$,
\eqref{eq:tail} with $T_m(1/z)\ge z^{-m}$ gives
$\eta T_m(1/z)-(1+u)^2\ge\frac14z^{3-m}-4>0$, because $(3/4)^{-10}/4>4$.
Optimality follows from the pairing after Lemma~\ref{lem:dualfactor}. Finally
$dV/dt=(du/dG)\sinh t/\sqrt{1+u^2}$ and $du/dG=-z^2u_z$, so $|V'|<1$ is the
inequality $u_z^2z^2(1-z^2)<1+u^2$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:p2curve}
Let $G(\zeta)$ and $u(\zeta)$ be given by \eqref{eq:p2param}. Then
$P_2(G(\zeta),u(\zeta))\equiv0$, where $P_2$ is the polynomial \eqref{eq:p2poly},

head: environment
name: The rational curve

title: Proof
body_md:
The identity is a polynomial identity in $\zeta$. The parametrization is
found as follows. Substituting $u=\sigma G$ gives
$P_2(G,\sigma G)=G^2\{\mathsf a(\sigma)G^4+\mathsf b(\sigma)G^2+\mathsf c(\sigma)\}$ with
$\mathsf a=32\sigma^2(8-16\sigma-\sigma^2)$,
$\mathsf b=-(\sigma^4+16\sigma^3+480\sigma^2-768\sigma+256)$ and $\mathsf c=-16\sigma^2$, a
quadratic in $G^2$ with discriminant
$(\sigma-4)^2(\sigma^2+32\sigma-16)^2(\sigma^2-24\sigma+16)$. The conic
$\varsigma^2=(\sigma-12)^2-128$ is rational, $\sigma=12+\frac12(\vartheta+128/\vartheta)$,
and on the root with the plus sign
$G^2=-64(\vartheta+8)^2/\{(\vartheta+16)^2(\vartheta^2+64\vartheta+512)\}$. The conic
$(\vartheta+32)^2+\chi^2=512$ contains $(\vartheta,\chi)=(-16,16)$; projecting from this
point and simplifying the parameter gives \eqref{eq:p2param}.

name: Data of the arc

label: lem:p2ids
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:p2ids}
For all $\zeta$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $K_6=\zeta^4(\zeta-2)^2+8(\zeta-1)^2>0$; hence $0<W<1$ whenever $e_-e_+\ne0$.

 -\bigl\{(1-c^2-u^2)M-2u(1-c^2)N\bigr\}=4G(1-W)\,(c^2+\mathsf ac+\mathsf b)^2,

name: Algebraic identities on the arc

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Expanding the right side gives $K_6$; its two terms do not vanish
simultaneously. In Definition~\ref{def:p2data}, $q_\pm=(\zeta\pm1)^2+1$, $r_+$ and

label: lem:p2ends
title: Lemma

name: Endpoints

title: Proof

label: lem:p2certs
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:p2certs}
Let $\zeta_c=1.69725$ and $\delta=0.00175$, so that
$\mathcal J=[\zeta_c-\delta,\zeta_c+\delta]$. Each polynomial $R$ of
Table~\ref{tab:p2signs}, and each irreducible factor of the numerators and

Theorem~\ref{thm:p2arc}, satisfies
\[

name: Sign certificates

title: Proof
body_md:
By Taylor's formula, $|R(\zeta)-R(\zeta_c)|\le\sum_{k\ge1}|R^{(k)}(\zeta_c)/k!|\delta^k$
on $\mathcal J$. The inequalities are finitely many comparisons of rational
numbers, $48$ polynomials in all. For the polynomials of
Table~\ref{tab:p2signs} the largest ratio of the right side to the left side
is $0.53$; the ratios up to $0.994$ occur for the decimal enclosures such as
$G<1.0337$.

label: thm:p2arc
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:p2arc}
For $\zeta\in[\zeta_1,\zeta_a]$ the data of Definition~\ref{def:p2data} have the
following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $G$ decreases from $G_1$ to $G_a$; $1.0233<G<1.0337$ and $0.511<u<0.517$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $-0.505<x<-0.48$ and $0.25<y<0.285$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $0\le p<1$, with $p=0$ exactly at $\zeta_1$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $0.362<W<0.366$, and $Q\ge0$ on $[-1,1]$ with zeros exactly at $x$ and $y$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $\bar g-|C|>0.28$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $\ell_1=\upsilon_2=\upsilon_3=0$; $\upsilon_5>0$ for $\zeta<\zeta_a$ and
$\upsilon_5(\zeta_a)=0$; every other raw slack is positive.
\par\hangindent 40\p@ $0<du/dG<1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently $V(t)=\operatorname{arsinh} u(\cosh t)$ for $G_a\le\cosh t\le G_1$, the measure $\nu$ is
optimal, and $|V'(t)|<1$ there.
head: environment
name: The arc $P_2$

title: Proof
body_md:
All signs below are read off from Table~\ref{tab:p2signs} on
$\mathcal J\supset[\zeta_1,\zeta_a]$.
(i) $dG/d\zeta=r_+e_-e_+/\{8\zeta^2r_-^2\}<0$, since $e_-<0<e_+$. The bounds are
the signs of $G-1.0233$, $1.0337-G$, $u-0.511$ and $0.517-u$ on $\mathcal J$.
(ii) $\mathsf b<0$, so the roots have opposite signs. Further
$1+\mathsf a+\mathsf b=q_-^3e_+/\{2\zeta r_-^2r_+\}>0$,
$1-\mathsf a+\mathsf b=-q_-^3e_-/\{2\zeta r_-^2r_+\}>0$, and $|\mathsf a|<2$ because
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 2-\mathsf a&=-\frac{\zeta^6-10\zeta^5+18\zeta^4-32\zeta^3+36\zeta^2-8\zeta+8}{2\zeta r_-r_+},\\
 2+\mathsf a&=\frac{\zeta^6-2\zeta^5+18\zeta^4-32\zeta^3+36\zeta^2-40\zeta+8}{2\zeta r_-r_+}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Hence both roots lie in $(-1,1)$. The finer bounds follow from the signs of
$c^2+\mathsf ac+\mathsf b$ at $c=-0.505,-0.48,0.25,0.285$.
(iii) $\bar c+\mathsf a/2<0$, so $\bar c$ lies below the midpoint of the roots, and
\[
 \bar c^2+\mathsf a\bar c+\mathsf b=\frac{32\zeta^3e_-e_+(\zeta^3+2\zeta-4)(\zeta^3-\zeta^2-2)N_{10}}{r_-^2r_+M_{10}^2},
\]
which is negative for $\zeta_1<\zeta\le\zeta_a$ and vanishes at $\zeta_1$. Hence
$x<\bar c<y$ on $(\zeta_1,\zeta_a]$, and $\bar c=x$, $p=0$ at $\zeta_1$.
(iv) This is Lemma~\ref{lem:p2ids}(a),(b) with $4G^2-1>0$; the bounds on $W$ are
signs of $W-0.362$ and $0.366-W$.
(v) $d>0$, because $D_{14}<0$ and $M_{10}<0$, and
$\bar g=1-u^2+\mathsf a\bar c+\mathsf b=8\zeta q_-^4N_8/\{r_-^2r_+^2M_{10}\}>0.28$. The
inequality $(\bar g-0.28)^2(G^2-1)>d^2$ is the sign of a rational function on
$\mathcal J$, whose numerator has one residual factor of degree $44$, certified
by Lemma~\ref{lem:p2certs}. Since $|C|=d/\sqrt{G^2-1}$, this is $\bar g-|C|>0.28$.
(vi) The three identities are Lemma~\ref{lem:p2ids}(c). For $m\le9$ the slacks
factor as in Table~\ref{tab:p2lags}, and every sign is determined by
Table~\ref{tab:p2signs}; all are positive except $\upsilon_5$, which has the sign
of $N_{12}$. For $m\ge10$, \eqref{eq:tailsharp} applies with $\bar g+2u^2<1.05$
on $\mathcal J$ and $\cosh mt=T_m(G)\ge T_{10}(1.0233)>4.369$, so
$\ell_m,\upsilon_m\ge0.28\cdot4.369-1.05>0.17$.
(vii) $du/dG=32\zeta^2q_-(\zeta^4-2\zeta^3-4\zeta+4)/\{r_+^3e_-e_+\}>0$, and $1-du/dG>0$ is
again the sign of a rational function on $\mathcal J$.
Optimality follows from the pairing after Lemma~\ref{lem:dualfactor}, with the
nonnegative weights $1,W,1-W$ on the active constraints. Finally
$dV/dt=(du/dG)\sinh t/\sqrt{1+u^2}$ and $\sinh t<1$, so $|V'|<1$.

head: environment

label: prop:p5divslack
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:p5divslack}
For a critical pair $(m,\sigma)$ let $s_m^\sigma$ be the limit, as $h\downarrow0$,
of the raw slack divided by $h$. With
$Y_m^\sigma(y)=(\frac34-y^2)(1-T_m(y))+\sigma(1-y^2)U_{m-1}(y)$,
\begin{align*}
 m\equiv0:&\quad s_m^\sigma=\tfrac{m^2}2-\sigma m(\mathcal B_0+D_0)+P_0Y_m^\sigma(y_0),\\
 m\equiv1,\ \sigma=-1:&\quad s_m^-=\tfrac{m^2}2+(\mathcal B_0-3\mathcal A_0)-m\mathcal B_0+mD_0+P_0Y_m^-(y_0),\\
 m\equiv2,\ \sigma=+1:&\quad s_m^+=\tfrac{m^2}2+(\mathcal B_0-3\mathcal A_0)+m\mathcal B_0-mD_0+P_0Y_m^+(y_0).
\end{align*}
These vanish exactly for the active pairs $(1,-),(2,+),(3,+),(5,+)$ and are
positive for every other critical pair; the smallest values are
$s_8^+=11.22\ldots$, $s_6^+=11.49\ldots$, $s_3^-=14.91\ldots$ and
$s_4^-=18.40\ldots$.
head: environment
name: First-order slacks

title: Proof
body_md:
Expand the raw slack to first order using $\cosh mt=T_m(1+h)=1+m^2h+O(h^2)$,
$\omega_x=\frac{2\pi}3+h\delta+O(h^2)$ with $\delta=-2\mathcal B_0/\sqrt3$,
$g(x)=\frac12+h(\mathcal B_0-\mathcal A_0)+O(h^2)$,
$2u\sin\omega_x=\frac{\sqrt3}2+h(\sqrt3\mathcal A_0+\mathcal B_0/\sqrt3)+O(h^2)$, $p=hP_0$,
$dU_{m-1}(G)=hD_0m+O(h^2)$, and, for the second atom,
$\sin\omega_y\sin m\omega_y=(1-y^2)U_{m-1}(y)$. Collecting terms in each residue
class gives the formulas. Vanishing at the active pairs is an identity in
$\mathbb Q(y_0)$. For $m\le7$ the signs are decided in $\mathbb Q(y_0)$. For $m\ge8$,
$|U_{m-1}(y)|(1-y^2)\le\sqrt{1-y^2}\le1$, so $|Y_m^\sigma|\le\frac52$, while
$|\mathcal B_0|+D_0<2.37$, $|\mathcal B_0-3\mathcal A_0|<1.81$ and $P_0<2.58$; hence
$s_m^\sigma\ge\frac{m^2}2-2.37m-1.81-6.45>0$.
head: environment

label: lem:p5tail
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Large lags near the three-cycle

title: Proof
body_md:
If $mt\ge3$, \eqref{eq:tail} gives
$\ell_m,\upsilon_m\ge\frac14\cosh3-(31/20)^2>0$, since $\cosh3>10$. If $mt\le3$,
compare with the three-cycle at $h=0$, whose raw slacks are nonnegative. The
term $\bar g(\cosh mt-1)$ is at least $0.49m^2h$. The change of the trigonometric
term of the main atom is at most $3h+mh/2$, by the bounds on $g(x)$, on
$2u\sin\omega_x$, and on the phase. The second atom changes this term by at
most $12h$, since its weight $p=hP$ is less than $3h$ and the two amplitudes
sum to less than four. The remaining constant term changes by at most $2h$.
Finally $|d|U_{m-1}(G)\le2.2h\,m\sinh3/3<7.7mh$, using $\sinh3<21/2$. Hence both raw
slacks are at least $h(0.49m^2-9m-17)>0$ for $m\ge24$. The bounds
$\cosh3>10$ and $\sinh3<\frac{21}2$ follow from $20<e^3<21$.
head: environment

label: thm:p5local
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:p5local}
There are $h_*>0$ and a unique real-analytic branch $Z(h)$, $|h|<h_*$, with
$Z(0)=Z_0$ and $F(h,Z(h))=0$. For $0\le h\le h_*$ the corresponding spectrum
is feasible and optimal, so that
$V(t)=\operatorname{arsinh}\bigl(\frac12+(\cosh t-1)\mathcal A(\cosh t-1)\bigr)$ for $\cosh t\le1+h_*$. In
particular $V$ is even and real-analytic at $t=0$, and $V(0)=\log\varphi$.
head: environment
name: Central family near $\kappa_c$

title: Proof
body_md:
Existence, uniqueness and analyticity follow from the analytic implicit
function theorem and Theorem~\ref{thm:p5h0}. For small $h>0$, $p=hP>0$,
$d=hD>0$, the weights are positive, and the dual quotient $q_2c^2+q_1c+q_0$
stays positive on $[-1,1]$, by continuity from $h=0$. The noncritical raw
slacks tend to $\frac32$, and the critical ones, divided by $h$, tend to
$s_m^\sigma>0$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:p5divslack}); this settles the lags
$m\le23$ for small $h$. Each inequality of \eqref{eq:centralbounds} holds
strictly in the limit $h\downarrow0$, after division by $h$ where appropriate:
$\mathcal A_0,\mathcal B_0,P_0,D_0$ satisfy the first four strictly; $u\to\frac12$,
$\bar g\to\frac12$, and $|C|=hD/\sinh t=O(\sqrt h)$; and, from the expansions in
the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:p5divslack},
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 h^{-1}\bigl(g(x)-\tfrac12\bigr)\to\mathcal B_0-\mathcal A_0=-0.773\ldots,\\
 h^{-1}\bigl(\bar g-\tfrac12\bigr)\to\mathcal B_0-\mathcal A_0+P_0(\tfrac14-y_0^2)=-0.267\ldots,\\
 h^{-1}\bigl(2u\sin\omega_x-\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\bigr)\to\sqrt3\mathcal A_0+\tfrac{\mathcal B_0}{\sqrt3}=0.742\ldots,\\
 h^{-1}\bigl(\arccos x-\tfrac{2\pi}3\bigr)\to-\tfrac{2\mathcal B_0}{\sqrt3}=0.298\ldots .
 \end{gathered}
\]
These limits lie in $\mathbb Q(y_0)$ up to the factor $\sqrt3$, and their comparison
with $\pm1,\pm2,\pm\frac13$ is decided as in Theorem~\ref{thm:p5h0}. After
shrinking $h_*$, Lemma~\ref{lem:p5tail} applies and covers the lags $m\ge24$.
Optimality follows from the pairing after Lemma~\ref{lem:dualfactor}. The
function $V$ is even by Lemma~\ref{lem:vmono}(i), and $V(0)=\operatorname{arsinh}\frac12=\log\varphi$.
head: environment

label: prop:p5arc
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:p5arc}
The continued branch of $P_5$ on $0\le h\le G_a-1$ consists of feasible and
optimal spectra, and $|V'|<1$ along it. At
$h=G_a-1$ it coincides with the endpoint of $P_2$.
head: environment
name: The central family

title: Proof
body_md:
The continuation starts from the exact point of Theorem~\ref{thm:p5h0}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:p5local} identifies the branch near $h=0$. On every slab the
enclosures give \eqref{eq:centralbounds} and
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 0.23<y<0.29,\quad 0.36<w_2<0.38,\quad 0.59<w_3<0.65,\quad w_5<0.031,\\
 w_5'<0,\quad |u_G|<1,\quad \sqrt{G^2-1}<\sqrt{1+u^2}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The endpoint value $w_5(G_a)=0$ and $w_5'<0$ give $w_5>0$ before $G_a$, and
$0<p=hP<1$. The quotient of $Q$ by $(c-x)^2(c-y)^2$ is a quadratic whose
coefficients satisfy $q_0-|q_1|-|q_2|>0$, so $Q\ge0$ on $[-1,1]$. For lags
$m<24$ all nonactive raw slacks are positive. Near $h=0$ they are evaluated
after division by $h$: a quantity is represented as $\mathsf c_0+h\mathsf c_1$
with its constant part evaluated at $h=0$, and the divided part is propagated
exactly through sums and products. For the main atom write
$\omega_x=\frac{2\pi}3+h\delta_h$; the mean-value theorem encloses $\delta_h$ by
$-\mathcal B/\sqrt{1-\xi^2}$ with $\xi$ between $-\frac12$ and $x$, and addition
formulas with the entire function $\operatorname{sinc}$ enclose the divided
trigonometric differences. The shifted Chebyshev polynomials
$(T_m(1+h)-1)/h$ and $U_{m-1}(1+h)$ have positive power coefficients. At $h=0$
every raw slack equals $0$ or $\frac32$. A critical slack, divided by $h$, is
its divided part; a noncritical slack, equal to $\frac32$ at $h=0$, is bounded
below, after division by $h$, by $\frac32/h_{\max}$ plus the enclosure of its
divided part, where $h_{\max}$ is the right endpoint of the slab. Lemma~\ref{lem:p5tail} covers $m\ge24$.
Optimality follows from the pairing after Lemma~\ref{lem:dualfactor}, and
$dV/dt=u_G\sinh t/\sqrt{1+u^2}$ gives $|V'|<1$. The endpoint identification is
the inclusion stated after Table~\ref{tab:p2lags}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Propositions~\ref{prop:p1} and~\ref{prop:p5arc}, Theorem~\ref{thm:p2arc}, and the
spiral certificate establish primal feasibility and the dual certificate on
all four arcs, and the pairing after Lemma~\ref{lem:dualfactor} identifies each
displayed curve with the boundary $u=\sinh V$. The endpoint identifications at
$G_W$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:p1}), at $G_1$ and $G_a$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:p2ends} and
\eqref{eq:p2endpoint}), and at $G=1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:p5h0}) make the boundary
continuous. On each arc $|V'|<1$: on $P_1$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:p1}, on the
spiral because $du/dG=1/(2G^2)\le\frac12$ and $\sinh t<1$ for $G\le G_W$, on $P_2$
by Theorem~\ref{thm:p2arc}, and on $P_5$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:p5arc}. Hence
$t\mapsto t-V(t)$ is continuous and strictly increasing, and it tends to
$\pm\infty$ because $V\le\operatorname{arsinh}1$. This proves \eqref{eq:scalarprescription}
and $\rho_{\rm HB}=e^{T(q)}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:spectral}. The spectra on the arcs have at
most two atoms.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The function $\Psi(t)=t-V(t)$ is strictly increasing and continuous, so
$T(q)=\Psi^{-1}(\log q)$ is continuous and strictly increasing in $q$, and
$q$ is strictly increasing in $\kappa$. On each open arc $V$ is real analytic
and $\Psi'=1-V'>0$, so the analytic inverse function theorem gives
analyticity of $T$ in $q$; the switching points are the values of $\kappa$ at
which $\cosh T(q)$ equals $G_W$, $G_1$ or $G_a$, which are the five points of
Table~\ref{tab:regimes}. At $\kappa_c$, $T=0$ lies in the interior of the
domain of the analytic branch of Theorem~\ref{thm:p5local}, so $\rho_{\rm HB}$ is analytic
there. Proposition~\ref{prop:spiralsub} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:classification} give $\rho_{\rm HB}=\rho_{\rm sp}$ exactly on the spiral regime
and at $\kappa_c$, and $\rho_{\rm HB}>\rho_{\rm sp}$ elsewhere; $\rho_{\rm HB}>q$ because $\rho_{\rm sp}>q$. The
expansions are proved in Appendix~\ref{app:finite}.
